label: models/fw_pipejunction.mdl: two pipes meeting at a flanged elbow, bolted

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, B, A, D where the asset was C, A, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief asks for two pipes meeting at a flanged elbow. The views show a vertical pipe rising from an elbow, with a horizontal pipe running off it in the LEFT, RIGHT and FRONT-LEFT views. The flange bands on both pipes and the octagonal elbow flange (FRONT, BACK, BELOW) are all in place, and no part sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size for the pipe junction, so there is no brief size to be within 15% of. Measured at 31 x 13.6 x 34 units, it is a plausible pipe-junction size and sits smaller than the crate-like device in lineup.png D, as a pipe junction should.

M3.reason: The named parts are all there: two pipes, a flanged elbow and bolts. Bolts are visible on every flange, 4 per flange in FRONT and 8 around the elbow flange in BACK and TOP. The elbow's rounded bend joins the two pipes at the lower left (LEFT, RIGHT). No named small part is missing.

M4.reason: The brief's palette is rusted steel. The pipes are a bright, saturated, mottled green (every view), which reads as moss or camouflage paint, not rusted steel. Only the dark grey flanges and silver bolts read as steel, so the main material is clearly off.

M5.reason: The mottled pattern on the pipes suggests wear, but it is green blotching rather than rust colour or streaks, so the 'rusted steel' wear the brief describes is not clearly there. The flanges have no visible rust or wear markings at all.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up rule. In the four readings the judges picked B, B, A and D, and the asset was caught only once (reading 3, where it was at A and A was picked). Under the rule it passes for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The brief sets no front. The piece stands upright on its vertical pipe, with the elbow and horizontal pipe reading as one coherent front (FRONT, LEFT). Its origin is not shown in the pictures, so this is not confirmed beyond upright.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors. At 384 triangles it is under the 422 that Half-Life's most-spending model of its kind and size uses, so it is within the amended bar. Pipe ends and flange faces read closed, and the parts are attached and not floating.
